content: The Zulip archive was last updated on Dec 20 2025. Is it because of an issue?

The archive is only updated manually using the scripts / workflows here and it looks like it has only been triggered twice. I think we're just keeping it around so that old URLs don't break, since Zulip now has web-public streams.

I see, the reason why I wanted to use it was for Claude to read a conversation in a topic. Claude wasn't able to read the web-public version because it requires JS to render the content. The archive is the only viable way. I will raise this issue to chat.zulip.org to see what they think.

Bryan Gin-ge Chen said:

The archive is only updated manually using the scripts / workflows here and it looks like it has only been triggered twice. I think we're just keeping it around so that old URLs don't break, since Zulip now has web-public streams.

I think @Eric Wieser's repeated contention is that the purpose of the archive these days is to ensure that messages are search-indexable. This isn't a thing yet even for web public zulip streams, it's tracked as https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/21881.
OK, I've triggered another workflow run. It looks like it could take a few hours.

Apparently, there is a Claude skill for fetching the web-public conversation: https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/137-feedback/topic/web.20public.20streams.20not.20readable.20by.20agentic.20ai.20tools
The job finished so the archive should be updated. I suppose it doesn't cost us anything to run it once a day (?) so I'll open a PR doing so later todya.
I think GitHub and Zulip will get annoyed at us if we do that
OK, I've opened archive#3 which would run the job once a month. Maybe that's more reasonable?

But I thought the archiving operation only fetches the new messages instead of fetching everything from scratch, i.e. the diff only. Running it once a week instead of a month means smaller diff each time.

Zulip devs have long wanted to turn the web-public view to be search engine indexable anyway. This feature will also enable the page to be read by AI agents.

The README in https://github.com/zulip/zulip-archive and the github actions file seem to suggest that we are using an official tool by Zulip (or more likely, this fork of it: https://github.com/eric-wieser/zulip-archive) to create the archive. The README states:

The above file tells GitHub to run the zulip-archive action every 20 minutes. You can adjust the cron key to modify the schedule as you feel appropriate.

If you Zulip organization history is very large (not the case for most users), it is recommended that you initially increase the time between runs to an hour or longer (e.g., '0 * * * *'). This is is because the initial archive run that fetches the messages for the first time will take a long time, and you don't want the second cron job to start before the first run is completed. After the initial run, you can shorten the cron job period as desired.

While I think a month is probably an acceptable frequency, this leads me to believe that Zulip might be fine with us running the archive more often. Or we can just ask them.
We used to be running it all the time -- was "web public channels" the only reason we stopped or did we get into trouble?
As I recall, we did get kind messages from GitHub support asking us not to force-push so much to some of our repos in the past.
I don't remember what was the outcome.
If the issue is force pushing, can't we instead just make new branches and delete old ones? Or is the issue that we are using github pages and deploying too often?
I remember it now. Github was unhappy with us storing the generated pages in git and force-pushing. The solution was to store the script only and use it's output as a folder for github pages.
